title: Track parcels that go off the end via sort confirmations (Gaylord destinations)
summary: When a parcel goes off the end of the sorter into a Gaylord at Hazleton, the system still generates sort confirmation messages that indicate two off-end destinations. Use those sort confirmations to track the parcel while it remains on the sorter, and rely on the system’s cleanup behavior once the parcel is sorted or rejected (removed from tables).
when_to_use: Use this when you need to track a parcel that has gone off the end of the sorter into a Gaylord at Hazleton, and you want to use the system’s off-end sort confirmations to follow it until it is sorted or rejected.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Identify the off-end condition and verify that sort confirmation messages exist for the parcel’s off-end destinations so tracking is possible.
access_or_tools_needed: Access to the live view/log where sort confirmations for off-end destinations are shown

access_required: Access to the live view/log where sort confirmations for off-end destinations are shown
system_preconditions: Parcel has gone off the end of the sorter into a Gaylord at Hazleton (off-end condition described by the source).

visual_references.description: Training video frame showing that a parcel sort-down triggers a divert/confirm/sort confirmation message (context for why sort confirmations are critical).

steps.title: Identify the off-end condition (Gaylord at Hazleton)
steps.purpose: Confirm you are dealing with the specific scenario where the parcel goes off the end into a Gaylord at Hazleton, which is the condition that still produces off-end sort confirmations.
steps.instruction: Using the live view/log you have for sort confirmations, confirm the parcel is in the off-end scenario described: it went off the end into a Gaylord at Hazleton.
steps.expected_result: You can associate the parcel with the off-end Gaylord-at-Hazleton scenario.
steps.healthy_condition: The parcel is clearly identified as having gone off the end (into the Gaylord at Hazleton) rather than remaining in normal chute/tote sorting.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot confirm the parcel is in the off-end Gaylord-at-Hazleton scenario, so off-end sort confirmations may not apply.

actions.label: Confirm off-end Gaylord scenario
actions.exact_action: Identify the condition described by the source: parcel goes off the end (into a Gaylord at Hazleton).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “off the end goes into a Gaylord at Hazlett... we actually get sort confirmations... two destinations... we can kind of somewhat track it... once it gets sorted or rejected, we remove it... from our tables.”

steps.title: Check for sort confirmation messages indicating two off-end destinations
steps.purpose: Verify the key evidence needed for tracking: the system provides sort confirmations that indicate two off-end destinations for the off-end Gaylord scenario.
steps.instruction: In the live view/log where sort confirmations are shown, locate the parcel’s sort confirmation entries for the off-end Gaylord-at-Hazleton scenario and confirm they indicate two off-end destinations.
steps.expected_result: Sort confirmation messages are present and show the parcel went off the end with two destinations (one of two off-end destinations).
steps.healthy_condition: You can see sort confirmation entries for the parcel that explicitly indicate off-end destinations (two destinations are referenced by the source).
steps.failure_condition: Off-end sort confirmation messages are not present for the parcel, preventing tracking based on confirmations.

actions.label: Locate off-end sort confirmations
actions.exact_action: Check for sort confirmation messages that indicate the parcel went to one of two off-end destinations.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if off-end sort confirmations are not present (source indicates tracking relies on those confirmations).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “we actually get sort confirmations... two destinations that they tell us it went off the end.”
“This message is pretty critical because if we don't get it, we don't actually know where it went or we don't know what's in the tote.”

steps.title: Use the confirmations to track the parcel while it remains on the sorter
steps.purpose: Apply the source-backed tracking behavior: off-end sort confirmations allow some tracking while the parcel is still on the sorter.
steps.instruction: Using the off-end sort confirmation entries you found, track the parcel’s off-end destination status while it remains on the sorter (the source describes this as “kind of somewhat track it”).
steps.expected_result: You can follow the parcel’s off-end destination information from the sort confirmations until it is sorted or rejected.
steps.healthy_condition: The parcel remains associated with the off-end confirmation information during the period before it is sorted/rejected.
steps.failure_condition: The parcel cannot be tracked because confirmation evidence is missing or no longer reflects the parcel’s current state.

actions.label: Track via off-end sort confirmations
actions.exact_action: Use the confirmations to track the parcel while it remains on the sorter (source says it can be somewhat tracked).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “we can kind of somewhat track it... once it gets sorted or rejected, we remove it... from our tables.”

steps.title: Verify cleanup after the parcel is sorted or rejected (removed from tables)
steps.purpose: Confirm the system’s expected lifecycle cleanup behavior so the tracking record is cleared once the parcel is no longer on the sorter.
steps.instruction: After the parcel is sorted or rejected, verify that the system removes the parcel from its tables (the source describes cleanup to keep the system clean).
steps.expected_result: The parcel is no longer present in the system tables used for tracking after it is sorted or rejected.
steps.healthy_condition: Post-sort/reject, the parcel’s tracking record is removed from the tables (no longer appears in the tracking dataset).
steps.failure_condition: The parcel remains in the tables after being sorted or rejected, indicating cleanup did not occur as expected.

actions.label: Confirm removal from tables
actions.exact_action: When the parcel is sorted or rejected, confirm the source-backed cleanup behavior: the system removes it from tables.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “once it gets sorted or rejected, we remove it kind of from our tables so that we keep the system clean.”

success_criteria: Off-end sort confirmations exist for the parcel and indicate two off-end destinations for the Gaylord at Hazleton scenario.
Using those confirmations, you can track the parcel while it remains on the sorter.
After the parcel is sorted or rejected, the parcel is removed from the system tables used for tracking.
healthy_conditions: Sort confirmation messages are present for the off-end scenario and explicitly indicate off-end destinations.
Tracking information remains consistent while the parcel is still on the sorter.
After sort/reject, the parcel no longer appears in the tracking tables.
failure_conditions: Off-end sort confirmations are missing for the parcel (tracking cannot be performed as described).
Parcel remains in tables after it has been sorted or rejected (cleanup did not occur).
escalation_guidance: Escalate if off-end sort confirmations are not present, since the source indicates tracking relies on those confirmations.
